text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When developers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate lines, and give variables clearer names. This process helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly without much care. Refactoring is not about adding new features or fixing bugs. Instead, it makes the code simpler and safer to work with in the future. Teams often refactor regularly, because clean code is faster to update and less likely to cause problems later.
